title: Ensuring Access to Clinical Trials Act of 2015
official_summary:
This measure has not been amended since it was introduced. The expanded summary of the Senate-passed version is repeated here.)

Ensuring Access to Clinical Trials Act of 2015

(Sec. 2) This bill amends the Improving Access to Clinical Trials Act of 2009 to repeal the sunset of, and so extend indefinitely, the exclusion from resources under titles XVI (Supplemental Security Income) and XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act, for eligibility purposes, of compensation in the amount of the first $2,000 per year received by individuals who participate in clinical trials for rare diseases or conditions.

summary.headline: Makes permanent a rule that lets people in rare-disease clinical trials keep the first $2,000 a year they are paid without losing SSI or Medicaid eligibility.
summary.what_it_does: Before this law, an exclusion let people in clinical trials for rare diseases or conditions set aside the first $2,000 per year of trial compensation when agencies counted their resources for SSI and Medicaid eligibility. That exclusion was set to expire. This law removes the expiration date, so the exclusion continues indefinitely.

who_it_affects.group: People who take part in clinical trials for rare diseases or conditions
who_it_affects.how: They can receive up to $2,000 per year in trial compensation without that amount counting against their resource limits for SSI and Medicaid.

who_it_affects.group: People who receive or apply for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Medicaid
who_it_affects.how: Trial compensation up to $2,000 per year is not counted as a resource when determining their eligibility.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 7, 2015; the summary does not state a separate effective date for the repeal of the sunset.
